title: Implicitly support auto-reflection for usages of cls.getDeclaredFields()

timeline.message:
Implicitly support auto-reflection for usages of cls.getDeclaredFields()

Fixes #1470

If a user invokes getDeclaredFields(), chances are they might want all declared
fields, and this usage will automatically add *all* declared fields to the
reflection data.
timeline.author: Bob McWhirter

timeline.body:
Fixes #1470

If a user invokes getDeclaredFields(), chances are they might want all declared
fields, and this usage will automatically add *all* declared fields to the
reflection data.
`getFields()` could be intrinsified similarly. It looks like `processGetFields()` is ready to accept it.
If the class doesn't declare any fields `getDeclaredFields()` could still be intrinsified to return an empty array constant.

Please refactor the code below, until the `pushConstant()` call, into a generic `getIntrinsicArray()` method. It can be reused for intrinsifying calls to `getMethods()`/`getDeclaredMethods()`/`getConstructors()`/`getDeclaredConstructors()` as well. (Feel free to extend this PR with those implementations too.)
Please also add a test for this. It should just verify that the call is indeed intrinsified by checking that a class's fields are accessible without the reflection config.
Thanks for the feedback. Wasn’t sure if this was a viable feature to add but I’ll shore it up and expand it now.

The only potential issue that I see with this feature is that there is no filter for which elements to register for reflection, i.e., it will register all fields of `Foo` if `Foo.getDeclaredFields()` is discovered even though a user might want to only add a subset of those fields (using the reflection configuration files method for example). Maybe we should place this feature behind a flag so it can be easily disabled.

@cstancu 

So, I'm hitting a wall.

`getMethods()` works with JNI enabled and disabled.

`getDeclaredMethods()` works only with JNI _disabled_.

When it's enabled, instead of getting a constant value node for the `Foo.class`, it ends up being an invoke graph full of `JNIAccessibleClass` and such seemingly bumping through `ToReflectedMethod` and such.

I've poked around quite a bit and can't find where the delta is between `getMethods()` and `getDeclaredMethods()` when JNI is enabled.

I'd welcome any pointers you could provide as to what mechanism I should be looking at.

timeline.body:
So, you can run the following native unit tests:

`GetFieldsTest`
`GetDeclaredFieldsTest`
`GetMethodsTest`
`GetDeclaredMethodsTest`

And all but the last pass. The last fails with an `NPE` due to somehow attempting to compile non-analysed code, ultimately from `copyMethods` within `getDeclaredMethods(...)` call chain. This seems to be happening because later on instead of a JavaConstant-able class, we have a `JNIAccessible.getClassObject()` invocation occurring, so the intrinsicification doesn't happen the 2nd time around. But the `copyMethods` doesn't end up in the ConstantPool, so the target method that isn't resolved is actually null, and the attempt to whinge about the unresolved method by name results in an NPE because a null has no method name.

*whew*

Oddly enough, if you find your way to `-H:-JNI` when running the test, then voilá, it passes and is happy.

So I've been unable to figure out why `getDeclaredMethods()` is the only one that triggers this thus far (I've not mucked with testing constructor reflecting yet), but not `getDeclaredFields()`.

Even when using a construct such as:

```
Class<?> c = Foo.class;
c.getMethods();
c.getDeclaredMethods();
```

within a single method, the first call to `getMethods()` always works, and resolves against the java constant for `Foo.class`, whereas the `getDeclaredMethods()` line immediately following, against the same local variable which should point to the same `Foo.class` is going via `ToReflectedMethod`/`JNIAccessibleClass`/the JNI dictionary stuffs.

Anyhow...

timeline.body: Reflection and JNI use separate data structures, so I don't see how JNI could directly interfere here. However, JNI's `ToReflectedMethod` itself calls `getDeclaredMethods` and `getDeclaredConstructors`. Could it be that state from multiple methods gets mixed up during intrinsification?

I honestly have no idea. Just instrumenting my plugin, the `receiver.isConstant()` returns false during one phase, because the receiver is an InvocationPluginReceiver representing an `Invoke(WithException)` around `JNIAccessibleClass.getClassObject()` as the argument for `getDeclaredMethods()`.

When that happens, it ends up attempting to compile through `Class.getDeclaredMethods()` and ends up barfing because `Class.copyMethods()` is missing from the constant-pool used by the `BytecodeParser` and not only do we end up with an un-resolved method, we end up holding a `null` and thus when it attempts to handle the unresolved, we get an NPE.

I have yet to figure out where/how `JNIAccessibleClass.getClassObject()` is being wired up.

But disabling JNI completely (`-H:-JNI`) allows the full build to work, and the result test-app to function correctly.
Any insight into this?

I'm debugging your code now. The unresolved method is `privateGetDeclaredMethods`, which apparently is never seen during the analysis phase, and therefore also not present in the hosted phase. I'll try to figure out why.

~~Actually, this must mean that the substitution code for `Class.getDeclaredMethods` is not used, since we replace this code.~~ My mistake, `privateGetDeclaredMethods` is replaced (and `checkMemberAccess`), not `getDeclaredMethods` itself.

I think our JNI code is merely triggering this problem because it uses `Class.getDeclaringMethods()` with a non-constant `Class` object, and the analysis seems to no longer be able to see through a non-replaced `getDeclaringMethods()` call, leading to its code not being detected as reachable and the image build failing due to these methods being unresolvable during compilation. @cstancu, since you are most familiar with the analysis, could you please look into this?

I really believe it is the wrong solution @bobmcwhirter and @cstancu. There are tons of code out there that iterates through all fields and members to find a subset of them. For example, find all methods annotated with @Inject for every registered bean/component. As I understand this patch would mean that every method and field would now automatically be registered?

If anything this should be opt-in and not opt-out, because unless you know it, you would never realize that all the methods/fields were included in the image.

Another question. What if one library requires that this feature is on, and another library requires that this feature is off? You would have no choice but to enable it.

I really believe that explicitly requiring people to add fields/methods is the right thing to do. If you allow implicit adding fields/methods it quickly turns into implicitly adding them for all of your code and every library that you use.

You could allow this to be enabled on a per-jar basis via a Manifest file. But it should never be a global switch.

As @kaspernielsen mentioned this could lead to too many fields being registered for reflection. We prefer that reflection registration is either explicit or it is the result of using the Native Image agent to profile the application.
